title: Runtime Semantic Versioning: Stability Guard, LTS Channels, and Migration Tooling
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a pragmatic semantic versioning policy and associated release controls for the runtime binary and HTTP API surface. It introduces the concept of a Stability Guard (automated compatibility checks + telemetry thresholds), formal LTS channel rules, and two pieces of migration tooling (compat-checker and rv-migrate) to reduce consumer disruption when we introduce breaking changes or deprecations.

Why now:
- We are increasing the cadence of runtime improvements (perf kernels, batching, new API fields). Without a clear compatibility contract and automated migration affordances, we risk repeated customer-impact incidents and costly rollbacks.

Policy highlights (engineer-facing):
1) Versioning model: runtime-MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where: 
   - MAJOR: incompatible runtime protocol changes (breaking wire format, auth header changes, major tokenization/response shape changes).
   - MINOR: backward-compatible feature additions (new query params, optional fields), performance ABI improvements that preserve request/response semantics.
   - PATCH: bugfixes, perf improvements, non-user-visible fixes.
2) Classification rubric for changes: every change must be classified in the PR body as one of [breaking, potentially-breaking, additive, no-impact] and include a short rationale and recommended migration path.
3) Deprecation windows: 
   - Hosted customers: minimum 90 days notice for additive deprecations, 180 days for breaking deprecations.
   - Dedicated/Private deployments: 180 days notice for additive, 12 months for breaking removals.
   - LTS releases: supported for 18 months from release for functional fixes + 12 additional months for security patches on request.
4) Stability Guard (automated):
   - Pre-merge: compat-checker (static analysis) runs on changelists to detect use of deprecated fields and client-facing surface changes.
   - Pre-release: run compatibility test matrix across pinned client SDKs and the smoke suite.
   - Post-release telemetry gates: staged rollout (canary -> cohort -> global). Health signals monitored: client error rate delta, latency p50/p95, token throughput, and a "semantic-regression" synthetic prompt set score. Any signal beyond thresholds halts rollout and triggers automated rollback.
5) Rollout gates (staged percentages & conditions):
   - Canary: 1% traffic for 6 hours; must meet <1% error delta and <5% latency regression.
   - Ramp: 10% for 24 hours; monitoring for customer-facing errors and quality regressions.
   - Broad: 50% for 48 hours; if OK then global.
   - Automatic abort if: error increase >3% absolute, latency p95 increase >20%, or semantic-regression drop >4 points on the canonical prompt set.
6) API compatibility headers and discovery:
   - Runtime will publish version metadata at /_runtime/version and support an Accept-Runtime-Version header for clients to opt into a specific MINOR or MAJOR-compatible variant.
   - Deprecation-Notice header on responses during deprecation windows with removal_date and migration_doc link.
7) Migration tooling: 
   - compat-checker: static analyzer that scans PR diffs and customer telemetry to produce a compatibility-risk score (0-100) and a list of likely impacted client code paths.
   - rv-migrate: a lightweight CLI that can rewrite common client callsites (deprecated fields -> new fields) for Python/TS SDKs and can generate a migration report for enterprise customers.

Operational expectations and docs:
- Every runtime PR that changes the public surface must include: classification tag, compat-checker report, a minimal migration snippet for each language we ship, and a suggested rollout gate (defaults above).
- Major/breaking changes require an RFC, a changelog entry, and explicit approval from the Release Manager and the Platform PM.
- Security-sensitive protocol changes require Security review and explicit opt-in migration assistance for Private installs.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Length of LTS support (18+12 chosen to balance stability and engineering burden). Can be revisited after first LTS cycle.
- Exact semantic-regression thresholds — current numbers are conservative; product to validate against historical releases.
- Whether Accept-Runtime-Version will be honored by Dedicated/Private by default or behind an admin flag.
acceptance_criteria: Documented classification rubric in contribution guide
compat-checker prototype runs in CI and produces risk scores for 95% of runtime PRs
rv-migrate CLI can rewrite two common deprecation patterns for Python and TypeScript SDKs
Canary pipeline implemented with automated abort on defined telemetry thresholds
Version endpoint /_runtime/version returns machine-parseable metadata and deprecation notices

2025-12-02 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed and suggested longer notice for private on-prem customers. Updated deprecation windows accordingly.
2026-01-10 - Morgan Reyes (SRE): Added concrete telemetry signals and abort thresholds based on recent incident postmortem. Refer: https://github.com/redwood-infer/postmortems/pull/88
2026-02-20 - Design review (Ava Patel): UX for deprecation header and /_runtime/version discovery agreed. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/designs/runtime-versioning-spec
2026-03-01 - Engineering review comment (Kenji Ito): compat-checker needs to integrate with SDK call-graph; assigned follow-up ENG-36290 to prototype call-graph extraction.
2026-03-04 - Release Manager (Noah Blake): Approved P0 priority. Requested addendum describing rollback playbook and on-call steps to be attached.
notes_for_ops: Rollback playbook to include: pause traffic in router, pin Accept-Runtime-Version to previous MINOR in gateway, trigger rv-migrate reverse step for critical customers, open incident bridge, and notify affected customers via the status page. We will attach a runbook once ENG-36401 completes.
